title: Re - Political Prisioners In S. M. Goal

page_data.en:
Re Political Prisoners in S.M. Gaol.

The political prisoners were placed in S.M. Gaol on joint
responsibility of Governor of the Gaol Sugai and Superintendent
Yamaguchi, officer i/c Foreign Affairs Section. Their safe
custody was considered by both officers and by Japanese
Gendarmerie as a very important task. However the political
prisoners succeeded in establishment of outside contacts within
comparatively short time. During February, 1943 a number of
arrests were effected among the members of the Gaol staff
on information received almost at once by gendarmerie and
Foreign Affairs Section. The information came to the notice of
respective institutions in four ways as far as it could be
established:

1. Sometime about the end of January, 1943 one of the
prisoners in the Gaol by the name Nicholas PAVLOFF
by occupation an ex-policeman dismissed from
S.M.P. was set free after completion of his sentence
for fraud. During his sojourn in Gaol he found out
about the connections with outside and utilised it
for improving his difficult financial situation.
He proceeded to one KASHIN, a Russian gendarmerie
agent of some standing and influence and a very shady
character and informed him that political prisoners
were planning an escape and established connections
with outside through some members of the Gaol staff
giving their names. KASHIN at once became very
interested and took N. PAVLOFF to one of his bosses
in BRIDGE-HOUSE. The information given by N. PAVLOFF
was rewarded with Ch.$5,000. N. PAVLOFF a heavy
drinker did not attempt to conceal his part in business
and openly boasted about his good luck to his friends
It must be presumed that a copy of his report was
duly passed to FOREIGN AFFAIRS SECTION.

2. J. BOURMAKINE, a warder in S.M. Gaol, was for long
time connected with one POORIN, a Russian agent of
considerable influence of Japanese consular Intelligence
department. J. BOURMAKINE escaped from U.S.S.R. in
1930 and was violently anti-Soviet in his views. He
became on account of these views pro-Japanese and
pro-Japanese. Having a good short wave radio set he
regularly listened to German broadcasts from Kiev
and as German frequently quoted the names of Red Army
units engaged in fighting made a list of those units
which were formerly stationed on the Far East.
It must be noted here that prior to his escape he
served a term of conscription in Red Army of Far East
and this facilitated his work. This list he presented
to one POORIN, mentioned above. As J. BOURMAKINE
stated later POORIN accepting this work and forwarding
it to his Japanese superiors attributed the credit for
the same to himself. POORIN promised to arrange

关于上海公共租界监狱（S.M. Gaol）中的政治犯。

这些政治犯被关入上海公共租界监狱，由监狱长菅井（Sugai）和负责外事科的主管山口（Yamaguchi）共同负责。这两位官员以及日本宪兵队都将确保他们的安全监禁视为一项极其重要的任务。然而，这些政治犯在相对较短的时间内便成功建立了与外界的联系。1943年2月期间，根据几乎立即被宪兵队和外事科获悉的情报，监狱工作人员中有多人被捕。据查，相关机构通过以下四种途径获知了该情报：

1. 大约在1943年1月底，监狱中一名名叫尼古拉·帕夫洛夫（Nicholas PAVLOFF）的囚犯，职业为前警察，曾被上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）开除，他在因欺诈罪服刑期满后被释放。在狱中期间，他发现了与外界联系的渠道，并利用这一渠道来改善其拮据的经济状况。他找到了一位名叫卡申（KASHIN）的人，此人是俄国宪兵特工，具有一定地位和影响力，但品行极为不端。帕夫洛夫向卡申透露，政治犯正策划越狱，并通过某些监狱工作人员建立了与外界的联系，还提供了这些工作人员的姓名。卡申随即表现出极大兴趣，并将尼·帕夫洛夫带往“大桥公寓”（BRIDGE-HOUSE）见其上司之一。尼·帕夫洛夫所提供的情报获得了5,000元法币的酬金。尼·帕夫洛夫是个酗酒者，并未试图隐瞒自己在此事中的角色，反而向朋友公开吹嘘自己的好运。可以推测，他的报告副本已按规定转交给了外事科。

2. J·布尔马金（J. BOURMAKINE），上海公共租界监狱的一名看守，长期以来与普尔林（POORIN）有联系，后者是俄国裔人士，在日本领事馆情报部门具有相当影响力。J·布尔马金于1930年逃离苏联，其观点强烈反苏。由于这些观点，他变得亲日。他拥有一台良好的短波收音机，定期收听来自基辅的德国广播。由于德军广播经常引用参与战斗的红军部队番号，他便列出了一份曾驻扎在远东的部队名单。值得注意的是，他在逃亡前曾在远东红军服过兵役，这便利了他的工作。他将这份名单提交给了上述的普尔林。正如J·布尔马金后来所述，普尔林接受了这项工作并将其转交给日本上级时，将功劳归于自己。普尔林承诺将来会安排

page_data.en:
for the latter's transfer to the Special Branch in some
future and meanwhile asked him for some more interesting
information. Probably on account of some vague rumours
existing among the members of the Gaol staff he became
suspicious in regard of some members of the staff and
employed one KURT MUCHA, a German refugee, to shadow
B. PETROFF. K. MUCHA was paid CR$10 and expenses for
his pains and submitted daily reports. It must be
supposed that his reports were sheer invention as nothing
incriminating was ever found against B. PETROFF. Due to a
blunder on part of some Japanese the part played by
J. BOURIAKINE became known to the members of the Gaol staff,
as a message was received and recorded by a British officer
on duty to send to headquarters J. BOURIAKINE and to
instruct him to bring with him his informer. J. BOURIAKINE
was well connected with K. Mehnert, German, editor of the
magazine "XXth Century", a German Secret Service agent.
It is also known that J. BOURIAKINE continued sending all
sorts of information to the FOREIGN AFFAIRS SECTION later
on account of which J. SEMENNIKOFF was subjected to
questioning. J. SEMENNIKOFF was also a member of the
Gaol staff and J. BOURIAKINE accused him in trying to get
an appointment in the FOREIGN SECTION of the Gaol with the
aim of establishing contact with political prisoners.

3. The position of E. ELIAS gave rise to suspicions. There are
no definite proofs to connect him with the incident with
giving information about his friend the other political
prisoners, but his general record is rather bad.
He was sentenced to the barest imprisonment at the same
time as the other men but 15 years for the same offence.
Nevertheless his sentence was some five times lighter than
that of the other men. The other political prisoners
always regarded him with suspicion. Upon his release he
immediately established excellent terms with Japanese
and was connected in suspicious matters, perhaps after
the war. He made attempts to form a secret organisation
among young refugees having come from China according to
Intelligence sent by one KAMADA (himself a Japanese
secret agent), was working for a cause. It might be
suspected that E. ELIAS intended to form a secret
organisation with the purpose of acting as a way to
Japanese head quarters. Acting as a Chinese Secret Agent
he was able to collect very much information. This is
trustworthy young people who came to him. This is
information undoubtedly true. At questioning
at the court he said that he knew well at the time
of KAMADA, who knew E. ELIAS well and at the time
lived with him in the same house and revealed good
deal of details later on.

4. During the stay of political prisoners in S.M. Gaol

3. E·伊莱亚斯（E. ELIAS）的情况引起了怀疑。虽然没有确凿证据证明他与向其朋友及其他政治犯提供情报的事件有关，但他的总体记录相当糟糕。他与其他几人同时被判刑，但因同一罪行仅被判15年监禁。尽管如此，他的刑期仍比其他几人轻约五倍。其他政治犯始终对他持怀疑态度。获释后，他立即与日本人建立了良好关系，并涉嫌参与可疑活动，或许是在战后。他试图在来自中国的年轻难民中组建一个秘密组织，据一名名为镰田（KAMADA，本身是日本秘密特工）的人发送的情报称，他正在为某项事业工作。有人怀疑E·伊莱亚斯意图组建一个秘密组织，旨在作为通往日本总部的渠道。作为一名中国秘密特工，他能够收集大量情报。这是那些信任他的年轻人提供的。这些信息无疑是真的。在法庭受审时，他说当时他很了解镰田，镰田也很了解E·伊莱亚斯，当时与他同住一所房子，并在后来披露了许多细节。

4. 在政治犯羁押于上海公共租界监狱期间

Iosif Borisovitch Fainberg, age 28,
Russian emigrant (Jew by nationality) N.F.A.
Police Hdqrs.          11-2-43.

    I was born in Harbin on April 28, 1913. At the age of 8
years, I entered a middle school in Harbin and graduated from it
in 1929 since when I was working as an apprentice in a fur company
(Shriro Bros.) till the end of 1931.
    In January, 1932 I left for Tientsin to join my parents
who were living there since 1930. I stayed in Tientsin until
1936 when I had committed a misappropriation and had to run away
to Harbin, where I lived for about 1½ years and then returned to
Tientsin as I was pardoned by my ex-employer. I stayed in
Tientsin only for two weeks and left for Shanghai in March, 1937,
and was living there till May, 1940. During this time I was
working as a salesman in the American Millionary Manufacturing
Co. Then for a while was a partner of a transportation company
(Commercial service Representatives) and after this was employed
as a sales manager by the Gunze Silk Manufacturing Co. during
which time (September, 1939) I was charged with misappropriation
and convicted to 6 months' imprisonment but appealed and was
finally acquitted of the charge. After this in May, 1940 I left
for Tientsin but was arrested there owing to my documents being
expired and was transferred to Peking where I was detained for
about 2 months and was then deported to Shanghai in August, 1940.
Since that time I was working as a salesman till January, 1942
when I was charged with larceny and convicted to 3½ years of
imprisonment. I appealed and finally was convicted to 1½ years.
    During my stay in the Gaol, I had many different jobs and
amongst them I was working for about one month (during December-
January) in the vegetable garden. Since January 8, 1943 I have
page_data.zh:
约瑟夫·鲍里索维奇·法因伯格（Iosif Borisovitch Fainberg），28岁，
俄国移民（犹太民族）无固定住所（N.F.A.）
警察总部          1943年2月11日。

    我于1913年4月28日出生在哈尔滨。8岁时，我进入哈尔滨的一所中学，并于1929年毕业，此后我在一家皮草公司（Shriro Bros.）做学徒，直到1931年底。
    1932年1月，我前往天津与父母团聚，他们自1930年起便住在那里。我在天津一直待到1936年，当时我犯有挪用公款罪，不得不逃往哈尔滨，在那里住了大约一年半，随后因得到前雇主的宽恕而返回天津。我在天津只待了两周，便于1937年3月前往上海，并在那里居住至1940年5月。在此期间，我在美国百万利制造公司（American Millionary Manufacturing Co.）担任销售员。之后不久，我成为一家运输公司（商业服务代表）的合伙人，随后受雇于郡是丝绸制造公司（Gunze Silk Manufacturing Co.）担任销售经理，在此期间（1939年9月），我被指控挪用公款并被判处6个月监禁，但我提出上诉，最终被宣告无罪。此后，我于1940年5月前往天津，但因证件过期在那里被捕，并被转移至北京，在那里被拘留了约2个月，随后于1940年8月被驱逐至上海。从那时起，我一直担任销售员，直到1942年1月，我被指控犯有盗窃罪并被判处3年半监禁。我提出上诉，最终被改判为1年半监禁。
    在狱中期间，我从事过多种不同的工作，其中包括在菜园工作了约一个月（12月至1月期间）。自1943年1月8日起，我

been in charge of dining room. At the beginning of January, 1943,
a group of "J" prisoners arrived amongst whom I recognized
Soulevitch and Rozenbaum whom I used to know before. On the
2nd day of their arrival whilst I was working in the vegetable
garden Soulevitch saw me and asked what I was charged with.
I answered him and then he asked me if I knew any way of getting
cigarettes from outside. I told him that this could be done
through Indian and Foreign warders. He asked me to find some one
who could do that for him. On the same day in the afternoon
warder Liaskovsky asked me if I knew any of "J" prisoners and
if any of them was a rich man. At the same time he told me that
once he took a letter outside from a Chinese prisoner and got
$2000 for this. I answered him that Soulevitch was quite a
rich man and that he is looking for a chance to communicate with
his wife. He told me to arrange the matter with Soulevitch
and he (Liaskovsky) will take out a message. Soon after that,
on the same day, I introduced Soulevitch to Liaskovsky and they
agreed that the latter will take out a message and bring some
food for a reward of $300. All this happened whilst the "J"
prisoners were taken out for a walk. On the next day about 1 p.m.
Liaskovsky told me that he had seen Mrs. Soulevitch and brought
plenty of food for her husband. He also gave me a pack of
cigarettes as a present, and told me that he received a letter
from Rozenbaum to his relatives and to one named .... Krivin.
During the following next days he was regularly bringing food
to the Gaol. Then one day he told me that from tomorrow he was
going on 10 days' leave and asked me to tell Soulevitch that

一直负责管理食堂。1943年1月初，一批“J”类囚犯抵达，其中我认出了以前认识的苏列维奇（Soulevitch）和罗森鲍姆（Rozenbaum）。在他们到达的第二天，当我在菜园工作时，苏列维奇看见了我，问我因何罪名入狱。我回答了他，然后他问我是否知道从外界获取香烟的途径。我告诉他可以通过印度籍和外籍看守做到。他让我找一个能帮他做这件事的人。同一天下午，看守利亚斯科夫斯基（Liaskovsky）问我是否认识任何“J”类囚犯，以及其中是否有富人。同时他告诉我，有一次他帮一名中国囚犯带出一封信，为此得到了2000美元。我回答说苏列维奇是个相当富有的人，他正在寻找机会与妻子联系。他让我与苏列维奇安排此事，他（利亚斯科夫斯基）将带出消息。不久之后，就在同一天，我将苏列维奇介绍给利亚斯科夫斯基，他们商定后者将带出消息并带回一些食物，报酬为300美元。这一切都发生在“J”类囚犯被带出去散步的时候。第二天下午1点左右，利亚斯科夫斯基告诉我，他见到了苏列维奇夫人，并为她丈夫带来了大量食物。他还送给我一包香烟作为礼物，并告诉我他收到了罗森鲍姆写给其亲属和一位名为……克里文（Krivin）的人的信。在接下来的几天里，他定期将食物带入监狱。然后有一天他告诉我，从明天起他将休假10天，并让我告诉苏列维奇

after his leave he will continue to bring the food. During
his absence Soulevitch asked me to find some one else and as
warder Novgorodoff was on duty in Foreign Section at that time I
suggested to him to see Soulevitch on the matter. Novgorodoff
immediately went upstairs and returned very soon with letters
which were already written by Soulevitch. After this for about
one week Novgorodoff was on duty in Foreign Section and during
this time brought food to the Gael on many occasions.

On Saturday (I cannot remember the date) rumours was
spread amongst prisoners that Novgorodoff got into trouble and
since that time he has not appeared in the Foreign Section.
A few days after Liaskovsky returned from his leave and told me
that he found out that another warders Koshman (No. 43) and
Novgorodoff were also taking out messages from Soulevitch.
He expressed his dissatisfaction at this and showed me Mrs.
Soulevitch's letter in which she asked her husband to deal only
with "Joseph" (Liaskovsky) as two others were unreliable.
She also wrote to him that she wished he will be separated from
Rozenbaum. Liaskovsky could not hand this letter to Soulevitch
in the presence of Rozenbaum, so he asked me to do that, and
I handed over the letter to Soulevitch on the next day when
they were taken down for a walk. On the next day Liaskovsky
told me that Gaol office discovered his dealings with Soulevitch
and demanded from him $2000 to keep their mouths shut. He also
told me that he already received $1000 from Mrs. Soulevitch
and asked for another $1000 from Mr. Krivin but the latter refused
to pay without a letter from Rozenbaum. Later on he went to see
page_data.zh:
-3-

休假结束后，他将继续运送食物。在他缺席期间，苏列维奇（Soulevitch）让我另找一人，鉴于当时诺夫哥罗多夫（Novgorodoff）狱警正在外侨监区值班，我建议他去见苏列维奇商谈此事。诺夫哥罗多夫随即上楼，很快便带着苏列维奇已写好的信件返回。此后约一周时间内，诺夫哥罗多夫在外侨监区值班，在此期间多次向监狱内的盖尔（Gael，注：此处原文为Gael，疑指某囚犯或特定区域/人员，依指令保留或按语境理解为向囚犯送食）运送食物。

在某个星期六（日期我已记不清），囚犯中流传着诺夫哥罗多夫惹上麻烦的谣言，自那以后他便未再出现在外侨监区。几天后，利亚斯科夫斯基（Liaskovsky）休假归来，告诉我他发现另外两名狱警科什曼（Koshman，第43号）和诺夫哥罗多夫也在替苏列维奇传递消息。他对此表示不满，并给我看了苏列维奇夫人的来信，信中要求其丈夫只与“约瑟夫”（即利亚斯科夫斯基）联系，因为另外两人不可靠。她还写信给他，希望他与罗森鲍姆（Rozenbaum）分开。由于罗森鲍姆在场，利亚斯科夫斯基无法将这封信交给苏列维奇，因此请我代劳。次日，当他们被带下去放风时，我将信交给了苏列维奇。第二天，利亚斯科夫斯基告诉我，监狱办公室发现了他与苏列维奇的往来，并要求他支付2000美元以封住他们的口。他还告诉我，他已经从苏列维奇夫人那里收到了1000美元，并向克里文（Krivin）先生索要另外1000美元，但后者拒绝支付，除非收到罗森鲍姆的信件。随后他去见

page_data.en:
-4-
Rozenbaum about it but did not succeed in getting from him
this kind of letter. Then he told me that he will try to
get this money from Soulevitch. After this, I have not seen
him any more.
This is my true statement.
page_data.zh:
-4-
罗森鲍姆商量此事，但未能从他那里拿到此类信件。接着他告诉我，他将尝试从苏列维奇那里弄到这笔钱。此后，我便再未见过他。
以上是我的真实陈述。

page_data.en:
Joseph R. Laskowski
Russia Poland
Police Hdqrs. 10-2-43.

I, the undersigned, Joseph Richard Laskowski, Polish citizen,
born at Vladivostok on the 14th of May, 1918. Arrived at
Shanghai with my mother and brother from Vladivostok in 1923.
My father, a musical master by profession, died in Shanghai
in August, 1942. My mother Nadejda Ivanovna (Pribovskaya),
age 57, residing at 151 Macgregor Road, my brother Vladislav
James Laskowski, age 27, unemployed at present residing with
mother at the above address. In 1936 I ended my studies at the
St. Francis Xaviers College after which I worked at the Joseph
Studio and later at the China Printing and Finishing Co.
I joined the Shanghai Municipal Gaol on September 1, 1941,
as an Assistant Warder No. 48.
I am sharing a room with B. Breva, Assistant Warder No. 6
at the Gaol's single man 's quarters, 147 Ward Road.
Whilst on duty at the Foreign Section about the beginning of
January at about 2 p.m. I was approached by convict No. 55 whose
name is Joseph Feinberg, this said convict asked me to do a
great favour for him to go up to a prisoner by the name of
Soulevich and help him in any way possible for which I will be
greatly rewarded this, as times are so hard now this greatly
appealled to me. I went up to see Soulevich about what I could
help him in, he at once approached me about informing his wife
about his presence in the gaol and at the same time gave me a
note to his wife telling her about his presence in the gaol more
or less a family letter. Then Rosenbalm seeing this asked me to
do the same thing for him and delivered a note to a Mr. Krivin
this was about the 3rd or 4th of January on that same night I
went to visit Soulevich 's wife and stayed at the house No.353
page_data.zh:
约瑟夫·R·拉斯科夫斯基（Joseph R. Laskowski）
俄罗斯 波兰
警察总局 1943年2月10日。

本人，下述签署人，约瑟夫·理查德·拉斯科夫斯基（Joseph Richard Laskowski），波兰公民，1918年5月14日出生于符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。1923年与母亲及兄弟从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。我的父亲是一名职业音乐大师，于1942年8月在上海去世。我的母亲娜杰日达·伊万诺芙娜（Nadejda Ivanovna，娘家姓普里博夫斯卡娅 Pribovskaya），57岁，居住在麦格雷戈路（Macgregor Road）151号；我的兄弟弗拉迪斯拉夫·詹姆斯·拉斯科夫斯基（Vladislav James Laskowski），27岁，目前失业，与母亲同住上述地址。1936年，我在圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xaviers College）完成学业，之后在约瑟夫工作室（Joseph Studio）工作，后来在中国印刷整理公司（China Printing and Finishing Co.）工作。
我于1941年9月1日加入上海公共租界工部局警务处监狱，担任第48号助理狱警。
我与监狱单身宿舍华德路（Ward Road）147号的第6号助理狱警B·布雷瓦（B. Breva）合住一个房间。
一月初左右下午2点左右，我在外侨监区值班时，第55号囚犯约瑟夫·费恩伯格（Joseph Feinberg）接近我，这名囚犯请求我帮他一个大忙，去见一名名为苏列维奇（Soulevich）的囚犯，并尽可能帮助他，为此我将获得丰厚报酬。鉴于目前时局艰难，这对我很有吸引力。我去见苏列维奇，询问我能如何帮助他，他立即向我提出，让我通知他的妻子他在监狱中的情况，同时交给我一张给他妻子的便条，告知她在狱中的情况，大致是一封家书。这时罗森鲍姆（Rosenbalm，原文拼写）看到后，也请我为他做同样的事，并递给我一张给克里文（Krivin）先生的便条。这大约是在1月3日或4日，当晚我去拜访苏列维奇的妻子，并在科恩路（Rte Cohen）353号

page_data.en:
-2-
Rte Cohen for a very long time as his wife was not in at that
time, she met me at the house upon arrival, read this letter
and in the letter he (Soulevich) was asking for some products
as he said that he was undernourished and at the same time he
asked for $300 to pay me which when she finished reading the
letter telephoned and the money was brought to her by Buck Frank.
We (Mrs. Soulevich and I) agreed to meet each other at Olympia
Cafe opposite the tram stop off Wayside and Muirhead Roads/
this she did and brought provisions such as sausage, ham, cheese
butter, cigarettes and matches together with cod liver oil,
then we parted. All these products were handed over to
Soulevich by me in the gaol.

When I brought these things over I was again in turn given
a note by Rozenhalm and Soulevich this time I gave them a pencil.
Soulevich was writing about how much some people owed him to
collect the money if possible and to write to him about the
results, whilst Rosenhalm was worried about his wife because
she is expecting a baby. This I phoned Mrs. Soulevich and told
her to meet me at Olympia again whilst the other note I brought
to Krivin off Rte San Zoong. Krivin gave me a note which I
did not understand being written in Russian but he told me
verbially about it (the note) that the price of cocoa is dropping
and that he sold a lot at a loss also saying that he is sick at
home, also stating about his wife 's health and to advise him
how much to pay her per month. Mrs. Soulevich and I met at the
Olympia and brought her over to the house (151 Macgregor Road)
after having some tea she gave me $150 to buy a few things for
page_data.zh:
-2-
待了很长时间，因为当时他的妻子不在家。她回来后与我见面，阅读了这封信，信中他（苏列维奇）要求一些食品，他说自己营养不良，同时要求给我300美元作为报酬。她读完信后打了电话，巴克·弗兰克（Buck Frank）将钱送给了她。我们（苏列维奇夫人和我）约定在韦赛德路（Wayside Road）和缪尔黑德路（Muirhead Road）电车停靠站对面的奥林匹亚咖啡馆（Olympia Cafe）见面。她照办了，并带来了香肠、火腿、奶酪、黄油、香烟和火柴以及鱼肝油等物资，随后我们分手。所有这些物品均由我在监狱内交给苏列维奇。

当我把这些东西带过去时，罗森哈尔姆（Rozenhalm，原文拼写）和苏列维奇又轮流给了我一张便条，这次我给了他们一支铅笔。苏列维奇在信中写道有些人欠他多少钱，如果可能请代为收取，并将结果写信告诉他；而罗森哈尔姆则担心他的妻子，因为她即将分娩。我打电话给苏列维奇夫人，让她再次在奥林匹亚咖啡馆与我见面，同时将另一张便条带给山佐ong路（Rte San Zoong，原文不清，疑为San Zong或类似路名）的克里文。克里文给了我一张便条，因是用俄文写的，我看不懂，但他口头告诉我便条的内容，说可可价格正在下跌，他亏本卖出了很多，还说他在家生病，并提及他妻子的健康状况，询问每月应支付给她多少钱。我和苏列维奇夫人在奥林匹亚咖啡馆见面，喝过茶后，我将她带到家中（麦格雷戈路151号），她给了我150美元，让我为她丈夫买一些东西，如

page_data.en:
-2.-

her husband such as sausage, ham, siberian cold lard, butter
and cheese which I did buy and deliver, at the same time Mrs.
Soulevich handed me $3000 for Pevzner, $300 for Soulevich or
more and about $150 to $200 for Rozenbalm. When this money was
delivered to the above mentioned persons in the gaol $800 were
given to me as a reward and the rest they kept for themselves.

Later on I came back and they, Soulevich and Rozenbalm gave
me another letter which I delivered both to Mrs. Soulevich and
Krivin. This time I gave them a pencil again but about the
paper I am not definite. Soulevich 's letter was sort of a
business like saying again that she should collect from a certain
Mr. Turchin some money and that he should pay some percent on
that money which he owed and he also asked if a certain Minko was
giving her money or not, whilst Rozenbalm asked about his house
property and that Krivin should give his wife sufficient money
to live during the time being these letters I gave to my brother
as I had no time to deliver them myself and he came back and said
that he did not receive any money from either of them but this
time only said that Mrs. Soulevich will come over to see some
of his China set (tea set) which she did not buy. I then sent
my brother to get some money from Krivin and Soulevich but
Krivin refused to pay only Mrs. Soulevich sent a $1000 in cash
with my brother. After this there were no more notes from them
or to them by me as I found out that some one else was working
for them for when my brother went to see Krivin he was introduced
to Rosenbalm 's wife and she stated that she knew everything about
her husband his health and whereabouts, but Krivin and Rosenbalm's
page_data.zh:
-2.-

香肠、火腿、西伯利亚冷猪油、黄油和奶酪，我照办并交付了这些物品。同时，苏列维奇夫人交给我3000美元给佩夫兹纳（Pevzner），300美元或多一点给苏列维奇，以及大约150至200美元给罗森鲍姆（Rozenbalm，原文拼写）。当把钱交给监狱内的上述人员时，我得到了800美元作为酬劳，其余部分由他们自行保留。

后来我回来时，苏列维奇和罗森鲍姆又给了我一封信，我分别交给了苏列维奇夫人和克里文。这次我又给了他们一支铅笔，但对于纸张我不太确定。苏列维奇的信有点像商业信函，再次提到她应向某位图尔钦（Turchin）先生收取一笔款项，并让他支付所欠款项的一定百分比利息；他还询问某位明科（Minko）是否正在给她钱。而罗森鲍姆则询问他的房产情况，并称克里文应给予他妻子足够的生活费。因为这些信件我没有时间亲自送达，便交给了我的兄弟，他回来说没有从他们任何一方收到钱，但这次只说苏列维奇夫人会过来看他的一套中国瓷器（茶具），但她并没有买。随后我派兄弟去从克里文和苏列维奇那里取钱，但克里文拒绝支付，只有苏列维奇夫人通过我兄弟寄来了1000美元现金。此后，我不再为他们传递任何便条，因为我发现另有他人在为他们效力；当我兄弟去见克里文时，他被介绍给罗森鲍姆的妻子，她表示对她丈夫的健康和下落一切皆知，但克里文和罗森鲍姆的

page_data.en:
-4-
mother-in-law were also quarrelling about something or other.
Once Mr. Roshmann (Ass. Warder 43) came to my room and asked
me if I was working that is bringing things to Soulevich I
answered in the negative but he found out from then that I was
bringing things to them and after I quit this whole affair after
the last $1000 from Mrs. Soulevich I did not want to go deeper
into this affair again and quit from that very last time.
But one morning whilst eating in the mess room, Mr. Novgorodoff
(Ass. Warder 39) offered to sell a bottle of Cod liver oil and
I bought it at $40 and at the same time seeing a familiar bottle
the same kind I brought to Soulevich so from that time I knew
that Novgorodoff was also bringing things to the Foreign Section.

This is my true statement.
J. Rachkowski
page_data.zh:
-4-
岳母也在为某些事情争吵。
有一次，罗斯曼先生（Mr. Roshmann，助理狱警43号）来到我的房间，问我是否在为苏列维奇做事，即运送物品。我予以否认，但他由此得知我一直在为他们运送物品。在收到苏列维奇夫人的最后1000美元后，我不想再深入卷入此事，便从那最后一次起彻底退出。
但是有一天早上，我在食堂吃饭时，诺夫哥罗多夫先生（助理狱警39号）提议出售一瓶鱼肝油，我以40美元买下，同时看到一个熟悉的瓶子，与我带给苏列维奇的种类相同，因此从那时起我知道诺夫哥罗多夫也在向外侨监区运送物品。

以上是我的真实陈述。
J·拉赫科夫斯基（J. Rachkowski）

page_data.en:
Joseph B. Laskovsky.
Poland
Ward Rd.Gaol    118243.

In addition to my statement given on 10.2.43, I beg to state
that the first time when I delivered a letter from Rozenbaum to
Krivin, I brought reply from Krivin to Rozenbaum and $300.00 cash,
which money Rosenbaum refused to accept, saying that you can take
the $300.00 for yourself as a gift.
I again confirm as in my previous statement that whilst
giving some goods to Soulevich, which his wife sent him PEVZNER,
Irakli(Kolotosashvilli), Vladimiroff and another cell mate were
sitting and talking about something or other , then Vladimiroff
together with Pevzner called me to their cell door and when I be-
gan to speak, Vladimiroff told Pevzner that he should be the spoke-
man and arrange with me what they were talking about, while I was
delivering the things to Soulevich; Pevzner then handed me a note st
stating that I should deliver this note to Mrs.Soulevich and she
knows were to get the $5000.00, which Pevzner is asking for, the
letter was written in Russian and to my misfortune I could not
read it but was only told verbally that I was to bring $5000.00,
which Mrs.Soulevich will get and on the following day I brought
them that is to say I do not know whether it was for Pevzner alone
or for all the other prisoners in the same cell - after giving them
the money I lingered for a while, then they Pevzner and Vladimiroff
asked me how much I was to get as a reward, but I could not tell
them the sum being involved in this affairs for the first time -
they then gave me $500.00 in hundred dollars notes and after a
while gave me another hundred dollars, i.e. $ 600.00.
page_data.zh:
约瑟夫·B·利亚斯科夫斯基（Joseph B. Laskovsky）。
波兰
华德路监狱    1943年2月11日。

除了我在1943年2月10日所作的陈述外，我谨补充说明，我第一次将罗森鲍姆的信交给克里文时，带回了克里文给罗森鲍姆的回信和300.00美元现金，但罗森鲍姆拒绝接受这笔钱，说你可以把这300.00美元当作礼物收下。
我再次确认如前次陈述所述，在给苏列维奇送去其妻子发送的物品时，佩夫兹纳（PEVZNER）、伊拉克利（Irakli，姓科洛托萨什维利 Kolotosashvilli）、弗拉基米罗夫（Vladimiroff）和另一名同牢房犯人正坐着谈论某些事情。随后，弗拉基米罗夫与佩夫兹纳叫我到他们的牢房门口，当我开始说话时，弗拉基米罗夫告诉佩夫兹纳，他应该作为发言人，与我安排他们正在谈论的事情；在我向苏列维奇交付物品时；佩夫兹纳随后递给我一张便条， stating（注：原文混入英文单词，意为“写明”）我应该将此便条交给苏列维奇夫人，她知道从哪里获取佩夫兹纳要求的5000.00美元。信是用俄文写的，不幸的是我看不懂，只是口头被告知我要带去5000.00美元，这笔钱将由苏列维奇夫人提供。第二天我给他们带去了钱，也就是说，我不知道这笔钱是仅给佩夫兹纳一个人的，还是给同一牢房的所有其他囚犯的——在给他们钱后，我逗留了一会儿，然后佩夫兹纳和弗拉基米罗夫问我应得多少酬劳，但由于我是第一次卷入此事，无法告诉他们涉及的金额——于是他们给了我500.00美元，均为百元面额钞票，过了一会儿又给了我一百美元，即共计600.00美元。

Translation from German

43

Albert Rosenbaum
Polish Jew self
11th of Feb. 1943. D.S.I. Sigerson.

I, Albert Rosenbaum, born on the 28-6-1900 at Lodz (Polish)
married, arrested by the Japanese Gendarmerie on the 5th of Sept.
1942 and transferred to Ward Road Gaol on the 31st of December,
1942.

After being here about 6 or 7 days and standing alone in
my cell, came to me an European Warder No. 48 and conversed with me,
he said to me that if I wanted something from my home he could help
me in that respect and mentioned the name of a person whom I knew
before, Csip. He then told me to write down what I need and he will
bring it to me and that I could write also a letter to receive from
there money. I wrote a note to give him from there $500.00. He
came on the next day and gave me some foodstuff, stating that he had
received $500.00 and I replied that I do not need money here and
that he could take it away. The paper and pencil was given by him.

In the note I wrote only to J. Krivin to look well after
my wife and also to sell all leather and goods in order to support
my wife with the money. I also added a note to my wife, in which
I wrote to her not to be angry with me and to take good care of
herself. Then, after a few days we were all transferred to another
block and I came together with four other persons in the same cell,
amongst them Mr. Soulevitch, when, after 2 days, another European
Warder No. 39, came to me in the same way offering his service
and giving me paper and pencil, I wrote the kind of Foodstuffs he
should bring. This note was for Krivin, in which I also wrote, that
if my child is born what name it should be given, I also wrote to
take away from Frank the diamond in order to sell them and give
my wife $2000.00 every month and also if he gets as far as that
page_data.zh:
德文译文

43

阿尔伯特·罗森鲍姆（Albert Rosenbaum）
波兰犹太人 本人
1943年2月11日。D.S.I. 西格森（Sigerson）。

本人，阿尔伯特·罗森鲍姆，1900年6月28日出生于罗兹（Lodz，波兰），已婚，于1942年9月5日被日本宪兵队逮捕，并于1942年12月31日转押至华德路监狱。

在此关押约6或7天后，当我独自站在牢房里时，一名欧洲籍第48号狱警来找我并与我交谈。他说，如果我想从家里得到什么东西，他可以在这方面帮助我，并提到了一个我以前认识的人的名字，Csip（音译）。然后他让我写下我需要的东西，他会带给我，并且我也可以写信从那里接收钱款。我写了一张便条，让他从那里给我带500.00美元。他第二天来了，给我带来了一些食品，声称他收到了500.00美元，我回答说我不需要这里的钱，让他拿走。纸和铅笔是由他提供的。

在便条中，我只写给J·克里文，请他好好照顾我的妻子，并卖掉所有皮革和货物，用所得款项供养我的妻子。我还给妻子加了一张便条，在信中我让她不要生我的气，并好好照顾自己。几天后，我们都被转移到另一个监区，我和另外四个人关在同一间牢房，其中包括苏列维奇先生（Mr. Soulevitch）。两天后，另一名欧洲籍第39号狱警以同样的方式来找我，提供服务并给我纸和铅笔，我写下了他应该带来的食品种类。这张便条是给克里文的，我在其中还写道，如果孩子出生，应该取什么名字；我还写道，要从弗兰克（Frank）那里取出钻石以便出售，并每月给我妻子2000.00美元，如果他能做到那一步的话，

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Albert Rosenbaum
native of Russia(Poland) taken by me self.
at on the 11-th of Febr and interpreted by D.S.I. Gigerson.

I, Albert Rosenbaum, born on the 22-6-1900 at Lodz (Poland),
married, arrested by the Japanese Gendarmerie on the 5-th of Sept.
1942 and transferred to Ward Road Gaol on the 31-st of December,
1942.

After being here about 6 or 7 days and was standing alone in
my cell, came to me an European Warder No 48 and conversed with me,
he said to me that if I wanted something from my home he could help
me in that respect and mentioned the name of a person whom I knew
before, Osip. He then told me to write down what I need and he will
bring it to me and that I could write also a letter to receive from
there money. I wrote a note to give him from there $300.00. He came
on the next day and gave me some foodstuff, stating that he had re-
ceived $300.00 and I replied that I do not need money here and that
he could take it away. The paper and pencil was given by him.
In the note I wrote only to J. Krivin, to look well after my wife
and also to sell all leather and cocoa in order to support my wife
with the money. I also added a note to my wife, in which I wrote
to her not to be angry with me and to take good care of herself.
Then, after a few days we were all transferred to another block and
I came together with four other persons in the same cell, amongst
them Mr. Soulevitch, when, after 2 days, another European Warder No
39, came to me in the same way offering his service and giving me
paper and pencil, I wrote the kind of foodstuffs he should bring.
This note was for Krivin, in which I also wrote, that if my child is
born what name it should be given, I also wrote to take away from
Frank the diamonds in order to sell them and give my wife $ 2000.00
every month and also if he gets as far as that to buy for the child
and to give the bearer $150.00. He returned and brought me foodstuff

Mrs. Anna ROSENBAUM.
Estonia Self
MP. H/Qrs. 14.2.45.

I am Anna Rosenbaum (Nee-Schonberg), Estonian, born in 1924,
in Howkden, dancer by profession, married and residing at 91/8
Rte Remi (Tel.72446). I was educated in Tientsin at St.Joseph school
In 1935, I arrived, with my parents, to Shanghai from Tientsin.
In 1939 or 1940, I have aquinted with Mr.Rosenbaum at Farren's
nightclub, where I was working as dancer of floor show. I married
Mr.Rosenbaum on 25.7.42, who at that time was a broker, working
with G.Krivin at 51 Canton Road. My husband was arrested by Japanese
Gendarmerie on 6.9.42. I had financial difficulties and knowing
that G.Krivin was a partner of my husband and had kept my husband's
money, I applied to him for money and Krivin supplied me on several
occasions from $50.00 up to $300.00. Later when Krivin was also
arrested by Japanese and soon after released, about December 1942.
Whilst my husband was detained at Bridge House, I have visited Ja-
panese Gendarmerie with a view to see my husband, what was not allow
ed and only some foodstuff and clothing, which I brought for my hus-
band were accepted and also twice I brought cheques, which was signed
by my husband and returned to me and this was allowed.

On 2 or 3 of January 1943, Krivin 'phoned to me and inform-
ed me, that my husband is now at Ward Rd. Gaol. Krivin did not tell
me where he got the news, but I think that was from Frank as he was
released. I applied to Police H/Qrs for permission to see my husband
and I was there few times, then about 7th January I visited Gaol
office and asked to see my husband, and also a cheque for $2000.00,
was signed by my husband and that was given to me right away, because
my house rent was not payed for 8 months. About the 10 of January
I with my mother visited Japanese Authorities at Kiangwan with a

安娜·罗森鲍姆夫人。
爱沙尼亚籍
警务处总部。1945年2月14日。

我是安娜·罗森鲍姆（娘家姓肖恩伯格 Schonberg），爱沙尼亚人，1924年出生于霍夫登（Howkden，音译），职业为舞者，已婚，现居住于雷米路（Rte Remi）91/8号（电话72446）。我在天津圣约瑟夫学校（St. Joseph school）接受教育。
1935年，我与父母从天津抵达上海。
1939年或1940年，我在法伦夜总会（Farren's nightclub）结识了罗森鲍姆先生，当时我在那里担任歌舞表演舞者。我于1942年7月25日与罗森鲍姆先生结婚，他当时是一名经纪人，在广东路51号与G.克里文（G. Krivin）共事。我的丈夫于1942年9月6日被日本宪兵队逮捕。我面临经济困难，且知道G.克里文是我丈夫的合伙人，并保管着我丈夫的钱款，我便向他求助，克里文数次向我提供从50.00美元到300.00美元不等的款项。后来，克里文也被日本人逮捕，但很快获释，时间大约在1942年12月。
在我丈夫被拘押于“大桥公寓”（Bridge House，即日本宪兵队本部）期间，我曾前往日本宪兵队试图探望丈夫，但未获允许；仅接收了我带给丈夫的一些食品和衣物。此外，我还两次带去由我丈夫签名的支票，这些支票被退回给我，这是被允许的。

1943年1月2日或3日，克里文打电话给我，通知我丈夫现在已在提篮桥监狱。克里文未告知我从何处得知此消息，但我认为是从弗兰克（Frank）那里得知的，因为他当时已获释。我向警察总局申请探视丈夫的许可，并去了几次，随后在1月7日左右，我访问了监狱办公室，要求探望丈夫，同时有一张由我丈夫签名的2000.00美元支票交给了我，因为我已有八个月未付房租。1月10日左右，我与母亲一同前往江湾的日本当局，试图

page_data.en:
- 2 -

view to obtain permission to see my husband or get from him a letter
so I left my letter there and was told come again within a week.
On the same day returning home from Klangwan, I was informed by
my sister that Krivin 'phoned to me 2 or 3 times and said that I
must 'phone to him as soon as I come back home, so I 'phoned to him
and he told me to come to his house at once, he received news from
my husband. It was about 3p.m. I visit Krivin's house at Empire Man-
sions on Rte de Say-Zoong and found in the room , Krivin, his wife
and another man, age about 28, medium build, that was the first time
I ever saw that man and the last, I didn't see him ever since, who
not a word handed me a letter from my husband written in English.
When I finish reading the letter and wanted to read it over again
but that man took that letter away from my hands and asked Krivin
if he wanted to read it. Krivin said no, so he took the letter and
went away. The letter my husband wrote was to let me take good care
of myself and that he married me because he loved me and trust that
I will be a faithful wife and told me that I am young, let me wait
for him and when he come out he will show that world to me and he will
make me happy then and that he don't mind my mother living with me
and said that if I need anything Krivin will always help me.

Krivin told me to prepare a letter for my husband and
take my photo and bring it to him and he will send the photo and let-
ter to my husband. 2 days later I brought it over to him and in
that letter I wrote that I am alright and the thing's in the house
are the same and that mother is taking care of me, and said that I
will wait for him no matter how long it will take, because when he
come out I want him to be the father of this child and be a husband
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

获得探望丈夫的许可，或从他那里得到一封信，因此我将我的信留在那里，并被告知一周后再来。
当天从江湾回家时，我妹妹告诉我，克里文给我打了两三次电话，说我回家后必须立即给他打电话，于是我给他打了电话，他让我立刻去他家，说他收到了我丈夫的消息。当时大约是下午3点。我前往赛宗路（Rte de Say-Zoong，音译）帝国公寓（Empire Mansions）克里文的住所，在房间里发现克里文、他的妻子以及另一名男子，年龄约28岁，中等身材。那是我第一次也是最后一次见到那个人，此后我再未见过他。那人一言不发，递给我一封我丈夫用英文写的信。当我读完信想再读一遍时，那人从我手中拿走了信，并问克里文是否想读。克里文说不，于是那人拿着信离开了。我丈夫在信中让我好好保重身体，说他娶我是因为爱我，相信我会成为一个忠贞的妻子，并说我年轻，让我等待他，当他出来时，会带我见识这个世界，让我幸福，并且他不介意我母亲与我同住，还说如果我需要什么，克里文总会帮助我。

克里文让我准备一封给我丈夫的信，带上我的照片交给他，他会将照片和信转交给我丈夫。两天后，我把信带给他，在信中我写道我一切安好，家中物品依旧，母亲在照顾我，并表示无论多久我都会等待他，因为当他出来时，我希望他成为这个孩子的父亲，并成为我的丈夫

page_data.en:
- 3 -

to me, and since then I did not hear any thing from Krivin
about my husband. I was again at Kiangwan and asked them if
I can see my husband, but told me to come after few weeks so
then I went to Japanese lawyer Dr. Y. Maki and he had fixed
everything up and he phone to me and told me to come to his
office and that he will go together with me to see my husband,
it was on the 8-2-43 I visited Ward Road Gaol with my Japanese
lawyer Dr. Maki and had official meeting with my husband, and
my husband told me that Krivin should pay me every 15th days of
the month $1,000.00 and if not, he should give the full account
to Dr. Maki, and the baby that will be born....let him be just
as it is not his religion and not mine.

This is my true statement.
(signed) Mrs. Anna Rosenbaum.
page_data.zh:
- 3 -

，自那以后，我再未从克里文那里听到任何关于我丈夫的消息。我再次前往江湾，询问是否可以探望丈夫，但他们让我几周后再来。于是我去找了日本律师Y.牧博士（Dr. Y. Maki），他安排好了一切，并打电话让我去他的办公室，他将与我一同去探望丈夫。1943年2月8日，我与日本律师牧博士一同访问了提篮桥监狱，并与我丈夫进行了正式会面。我丈夫告诉我，克里文应在每月15日支付我1,000.00美元，否则应向牧博士提交完整账目；至于即将出生的孩子……就顺其自然吧，既非他的宗教，也非我的宗教。

以上是我的真实供词。
（签名）安娜·罗森鲍姆夫人。

I, the undersigned, ~~PRIMER~~ Jacov Alexandrovich, citizen of USSR.,
29 years of age, married. I was arrested by Japanese Gendarmerie
on 25:10.42, and was transferred to Ward Rd. Gaol on 31:12:42.
2 or 3 days after my arrival to Gaol, cells where I was detained
was visited by one named Roman STARKOVSKY, who served as dresser
for convicts in Gaol, and whom I regarded as officially appointed
Gaol employee (he was taking down particulars of our medical ex-
amination in the office on the day of our arrival at Gaol) and
Starkovsky offered to all prisoners, if any one desired to write
letters to their relatives, these letters can be delivered to whom
they are addressed, through his service. 3 prisoners, who were in
cells with me refused, as they were waiting official permission
for meeting with their relatives. My family in USSR, and I had no
news from them for about 6 months and myself had no chance to in-
form them about myself, I have decided to write, being sure, that my
letter will be forwarded officially, through the Gaol's Administra-
tion. Starkovsky gave me a pencil and paper and I wrote a letter to
my wife, which letter I asked Starkovsky to deliver to "Experthleb"
wherefrom this letter to be sent through the post, to my wife.
When 2 days latter Starkovsky again visited our cells, I asked him
about my letter and he told me that he did not yet delivered my
letter, because his mother did not come to see him. From this talk
I found out, that Starkovsky himself is a prisoner and my letter
he was going out to sent by not official way, and I asked him to
return me my letter. On the other day when I repeated my request
Starkovsky told me, that he already destroyed my letter. After this
case I did not apply to anybody and nobody approached me regarding
letters. During my detention here I did not receive any letters

苏联
提篮桥监狱    1943年2月11日。    D.S.科切托夫（D.S. Kochetoff）。
本人，下述签署人，雅科夫·亚历山德罗维奇·佩夫斯纳（Jacov Alexandrovich Pevsner，原文此处有涂改痕迹，结合下文签名应为Pevsner），苏联公民，29岁，已婚。我于1942年10月25日被日本宪兵队逮捕，并于1942年12月31日被移送至提篮桥监狱。
抵达监狱两三天后，一名名叫罗曼·斯塔科夫斯基（Roman STARKOVSKY）的人探访了我所在的牢房，他在狱中担任囚犯服务员，我视其为官方任命的监狱雇员（在我们抵达监狱当天，他曾在办公室记录我们的体检详情）。斯塔科夫斯基向所有囚犯提议，如果有人希望给亲属写信，可以通过他的服务将信件送达收件人。与我同牢房的三名囚犯拒绝了，因为他们正在等待与亲属会面的官方许可。我的家人在苏联，我已约有六个月没有他们的消息，我自己也没有机会向他们通报我的情况，我决定写信，确信我的信会通过监狱管理部门官方转发。斯塔科夫斯基给了我铅笔和纸，我写了一封给妻子的信，并请斯塔科夫斯基将信送至“Experthleb”（音译，可能指某机构或地点），以便由此通过邮政寄给我的妻子。
两天后，斯塔科夫斯基再次探访我们的牢房，我向他询问我的信的情况，他告诉我尚未投递我的信，因为他的母亲没来看他。通过这次谈话，我发现斯塔科夫斯基本身也是一名囚犯，他打算通过非官方渠道寄出我的信，于是我要求他退还我的信。次日，当我再次提出请求时，斯塔科夫斯基告诉我，他已经销毁了我的信。此事之后，我没有再向任何人提出申请，也没有人就此事宜接触我。在被拘押期间，我没有收到任何信件

page_data.en:
-2-

or money and I did not see that other prisoners received letters
or money. I, together with other prisoners officially received
one parcel with products.

This is my true statement
( signed ) Pevsner.
